atm: Assalamu alaikum! Our model is a Halal Finance ATM. In Islam, money is an amanah, a trust from Allah. Every button on this machine shows how a Muslim should use that trust.
The key verse is Surah Al-Baqarah 2:275: 'Allah has permitted trade and has forbidden interest.' Our whole ATM is built around this difference.
This is our Zakat calculator. We enter savings, gold and debts. If the total is above the nisab for a full lunar year, 2.5% is due. Here it calculates the zakat instantly.
Surah At-Tawbah 9:60 names eight groups who receive zakat, including the poor, the needy, people in debt and stranded travellers. Zakat is not a gift; it is their right.
The Riba Check compares an interest loan with a halal Murabaha sale. Watch the interest bar: if you pay late it keeps growing. The halal price is fixed and never grows.
In Sahih Muslim 1598, the Prophet ﷺ cursed the one who takes interest, the one who pays it, the one who writes it and the two witnesses, and said they are all equal.
Now the Sadaqah button. Each coin flies to a cause, like clean water or food. Surah Al-Baqarah 2:261 says charity is like one seed growing into seven hundred grains.
Finally, our sorting game. Is this transaction halal or haram? We will now test you with a quick quiz. Thank you for listening!
sky: Assalamu alaikum! Our model is Sky Shield. This is the Earth, surrounded by transparent shells. Each shell is a layer of the atmosphere. The layers are enlarged so you can see them.
In Surah Al-Anbiya 21:32, Allah says: 'And We made the sky a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs, are turning away.' Now let's look at the science separately.
The lowest layer is the troposphere, up to about 12 km. Almost all clouds, rain and storms happen here. It holds most of the air we breathe.
These purple rays are ultraviolet light from the Sun. The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs all UV-C and most UV-B. Watch what happens when I switch the ozone off: the rays reach the ground.
Now let's launch meteors. They hit the atmosphere at huge speed, glow, and burn up before they reach us. Dozens of tonnes of space dust enter every day.
Most meteors burn up in the mesosphere, about 50 to 85 km up. It is the coldest layer, around minus 90 degrees Celsius at the top.

Higher up are the thermosphere, with auroras and the Space Station, and the exosphere, which fades into space. In 86:11 Allah swears by 'the sky which returns', which scholars explained as returning rain.
So the next time you check the UV index or see a shooting star, remember the protected ceiling above us. Now let's try a quick quiz. Thank you!
waqf: Assalamu alaikum! Our model is about waqf, a charity that keeps giving. A waqf is an asset given for Allah's sake: the asset is kept forever, and only its benefit is given away.
In Sahih al-Bukhari 2737, Umar got the best land he had ever owned. The Prophet ﷺ advised: keep it as an endowment and give its yield in charity. It could never be sold, gifted or inherited.
Now we donate a water well to the village. Look at the counter: in the first year, the families nearby start drinking clean water.
Let's drag the timeline to fifty years. The village has grown, the children have grown up, and the well is still working. The trustee has repaired it from its own income.
At one hundred and fifty years, five generations have used the same well. The counter has passed many thousands of people, and the donor is still being rewarded.
Sahih Muslim 1631: when a person dies, their deeds end except three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, and a righteous child who prays for them. A waqf is the best example of ongoing charity.

If we donate a school instead and go to three hundred years, it is like al-Qarawiyyin University, founded by Fatima al-Fihri in 859 and still teaching today. Surah Aal-Imran 3:92 says to give from what you love.
You don't need to be rich. Planting a tree or donating books can become ongoing charity. Now let's try a quick quiz. Thank you for listening!
clock: Assalamu alaikum! Our model is the Cosmic Clock: the Sun, the Earth and the Moon. Surah Ar-Rahman 55:5 says: 'The sun and the moon move by precise calculation.'
Surah Yunus 10:5 calls the Sun a 'shining light' and the Moon a 'derived light'. Science confirms the Sun makes light by fusion, while the Moon only reflects sunlight.
Using the time slider, here is day 1. A thin crescent appears after sunset, and that starts a new Hijri month. Surah Al-Baqarah 2:189 says new moons are measurements of time.
Dragging to day 14 or 15, the Moon is on the far side of Earth from the Sun, so we see its whole lit face: a full moon. A full cycle takes about 29.5 days.
Near day 27 the Moon becomes a thin curved crescent again. Surah Ya-Sin 36:39 says it returns 'like the old date stalk', which is thin and curved, exactly this shape.
Now Prayer Times mode. As Earth spins, the Sun climbs. When it passes its highest point it's Dhuhr. Later, when shadows lengthen, it's Asr.
At sunset it's Maghrib. When twilight disappears it's Isha, and Fajr begins at dawn. Surah An-Nisa 4:103: prayer is decreed at specified times.
Finally, the orbit toggle. Each body moves in its own path. Surah Ya-Sin 36:40 says 'each, in an orbit, is swimming.' Now a quick quiz. Thank you!
market: Assalamu alaikum! Our model is an Islamic Business Investment Simulator. Surah An-Nisa 4:29 tells us to trade only by mutual consent and never take wealth unjustly.
Before investing, we screen the business. Let's click the casino: it's rejected, because Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:90 forbids gambling and intoxicants. The same goes for the liquor shop.
The bakery passes screening. We choose Mudarabah: the investor gives the money, the baker gives the skill, and they agree to share profit 60 to 40.
Let's simulate a good year. The bakery makes a profit, and both partners receive their agreed share. Watch the coin towers grow.
Now a bad year: sales drop and there's a loss. In Mudarabah the investor's money carries the loss, while the baker loses their effort. Nobody is forced into debt.
With Musharakah, both partners invest money. Profit is shared by agreement, and losses are shared by how much each person invested. It's a true partnership.
Here is the side-by-side comparison. With an interest loan, the lender gets paid even in a bad year and the borrower carries all the risk. Allah permitted trade and forbade interest, 2:275.
Even a school bake sale can follow these rules. Now let's try the quick quiz. Thank you for listening!
ocean: Assalamu alaikum! Welcome aboard our Ocean Depth Explorer. In Surah An-Nur 24:40, Allah describes 'darknesses within an unfathomable sea, covered by waves, upon which are waves, over which are clouds.'
Look: surface waves on top, and below them internal waves where warm and cold water layers meet. They are hidden underwater, and some are over 100 metres tall.
As we dive, watch the colour bar. Red disappears by about 10 metres, then orange, then yellow. At 60 metres, everything already looks blue-green.
At 500 metres, the twilight zone, only faint blue light is left. No plants grow here. Lanternfish make their own light.
At 2,000 metres, the midnight zone, there is total darkness. As the verse says, if you put out your hand you can hardly see it. We need the submarine's lights.
Down to almost 11,000 metres, the Challenger Deep. The pressure is over a thousand times that at the surface. Allah's creation reaches places humans have barely explored.

Now the Two Seas scene. Fresh river water meets salty sea water. Surah Al-Furqan 25:53 says one is fresh and sweet, one salty and bitter, with a barrier between them. Scientists call this zone a halocline.
The deep sea's darkness is a parable for life without guidance, and the Qur'an is our light. Now let's try a quick quiz. Thank you!
